newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Next says margins up slightly.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Next says margins up slightly.

text.p: Retailer Next Plc said gross margins rose very slightly in both its stores and mail order business in the first half.
Chief executive David Jones said selling prices were slightly down because of negligible price inflation.
"In general our average selling prices are marginally lower than last year because there's very minor price inflation," he said in a telephone interview.
Costs were under reasonable control, with no repeat of last year's big increase in paper costs, he said. Wage costs were up about 3.5 percent and rents were not showing any major rise.
The group, which earlier reported first half pretax profits of 56.0 million stg, had net cash of 143 million stg at the half year.

Jones said Next was quite relaxed about having a cash mountain, which would be used to fund its progressive dividend policy and also for investment in its warehouse reorganisation, due for completion by end 1997.
"We don't have to go running to banks to do what we want to do," he said, "We don't feel embarrassed by having 140 odd million."
Jones dismissed speculation that the appointment of Next chairman Lord Wolfson as chairman of Great Universal Stores Plc might lead to a link-up between the two retailers.
"I don't really think that there's anything on the horizon at the moment, not as far as I'm aware."
Next's 20 franchises overseas are doing well and Jones said the group plans to open another 10 before the year-end.
In the U.S., where the group has four stores, Next said it had no current plans for expansion although the business was steadily improving.
The chief executive said the performance from its store in France had been disappointing and there were no plans to open any more.
He said the group would wait and see how it traded in the run up to Christmas before making any decisions on further expansion.

Jones said the retail climate in general had improved in the first half. "There is a general improvement in trade. What people are comparing with are the crazy days of 10 years ago -- obviously we're not doing as well as then." -- Jane Merriman +44 171 542 7717
